transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh… I guess they brought me in because of work. At the warehouse. People keep saying I’m doing things wrong, but the boxes have a kind of order if you look at them right, like little roads, you know? 

Sometimes I’ll just stop by the forklift with my arms up, and they yell because it’s in the way, and I copy the beeping sounds or the hand signals the guys do. It’s not really… I don’t know, it just happens. They get mad and tell me to stop moving boxes into patterns when I’m supposed to be loading them.
Do you think the patterns you see in the boxes are real, or are they just something you imagine?

I don’t know… I mean, the boxes are real, obviously, you can touch them, and the tape lines and labels, they line up sometimes. But if you mean like, does everybody see it the way I do, I don’t know. 

At the warehouse they just want them stacked fast, like blue pallet over here, damaged ones over there, and I try to explain it’s cleaner if the corners match, like when you’re lining up notebooks for class— I used to do that, keep the edges straight. So… I’m not sure if it’s imagined. It feels like it’s there when I’m looking at it.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds when no one else is around?

I don’t know… sounds, yeah, there’s always sounds, like the building makes noises even when it’s quiet, the lights buzz and the carts kind of squeak in my head after work. Voices though… I mean, if someone’s not there? I don’t really know how you’d tell for sure.

Sometimes I think I hear my name, but then it could be the hallway or somebody outside, or like when the forklift backs up and the beep gets stuck in your ears. My old dorm had pipes that sounded like people talking, too, especially at night. So… I haven’t really noticed it in a clear way, I guess.
Do you believe that the patterns you see in the boxes have a special meaning or purpose?

Special meaning… I don’t know if I’d call it special. It’s more like… if the boxes line up wrong, it feels messy, like when a song is off-beat. But purpose, I mean, everything in the warehouse has a purpose, right? Labels, numbers, where stuff goes.

Sometimes I think if I put them the right way it makes more sense, but I don’t know that it means anything beyond that. My old notebooks used to be like that too, all the corners even, and if someone borrowed one and bent the pages I’d keep thinking about it. So… I’m not sure. It just feels like there’s a right way they should be.
Do you think someone or something is controlling your actions when you arrange the boxes into patterns?

Controlling… I don’t know. I don’t think of it like someone with a remote or anything. I’m just trying to get them right, like the edges and the labels, because if one is turned weird it kind of pulls my attention.

But “something” controlling it… I mean, work kind of controls it too, because the scanner tells you where things go, and the supervisor wants it fast, and then you start moving without thinking. Like when I used to walk to class and suddenly you’re there and you don’t remember every step. So… I’m not sure that’s what you mean. I haven’t really noticed someone making me do it.
Do you ever feel like you can't stop thinking about arranging the boxes into patterns, even when you're not at work?

I mean… I don’t know. Sometimes after work I still see the stacks in my head, like when you’ve been staring at something too long and then you close your eyes and it’s still kind of there. But I don’t know if that’s the same as not being able to stop thinking about it.

Like, when I was in school, after doing math homework, I’d keep seeing the numbers for a while, or if a song is playing at the store it gets stuck in your head even if you don’t like it. The boxes are kind of like that maybe. I haven’t really… noticed it in a way where I’d say it takes over or something. It’s just there sometimes, I guess.
Do you feel like your way of arranging the boxes or thinking about patterns is causing problems for you in your daily life?

Yeah… I guess it is. I mean, I didn’t think it was like a “problem” problem at first, just me trying to do the job right, but then they took me off the forklift. They said it wasn’t safe, or that I was getting too distracted with where things were set, and… I don’t know, I used to be good with the forklift.

And school too, I’m behind in my community college classes. I’ll sit down to do the work and then I start thinking about rows and labels and how things should line up, and then it’s like the whole evening is gone. It reminds me of when my uncle would organize his garage by color, but he could still find everything, so I don’t know why mine turns into such a mess.

I also stopped going to the church food-bank shifts. People there were saying they couldn’t count on me, or they didn’t feel like things were safe around me anymore. That one kind of… yeah, that bothered me. I liked helping there. So I guess it’s causing problems, even if I don’t always see it happening right away.
Do you feel like you're thinking about arranging the boxes into patterns even when you don't want to?

I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t sit there and think, “I don’t want to think about boxes,” exactly. It’s more like my mind goes there if something reminds me, like if I see shelves at a store or the way cereal boxes are lined up, and then I start noticing which one is crooked.

But I don’t know if that counts as even when I don’t want to. Sometimes I’m trying to do school stuff and it pops in, but then I also end up thinking about other things too, like whether I paid my phone bill or what time the bus comes. The bus route near my apartment changed and now the timing is all off, so I have to leave earlier, and that kind of messes up the whole day.

So… yeah, I guess it happens when I’m not trying to think about it, but I don’t know if I’d say I “don’t want to.” It’s just there sometimes.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop thinking about the patterns, even when you try to focus on something else?

I don’t know if I’d say “unable,” exactly. Like, sometimes I try to read for class and then I realize I’m thinking about how the page is laid out, or how the boxes at work would fit better if they were turned the other way, but then… I don’t know, everybody’s mind wanders, right?

It’s kind of like when my roommate keeps the dishes in the wrong cabinet and then I’ll think about that while I’m supposed to be doing something else. But then I’ll also think about the bus schedule, or whether I left my work gloves in my locker, or that time the labels got put on the wrong pallets and nobody noticed until the end of the shift.

So… I guess I notice the patterns come up when I’m trying to focus, but I’m not sure if that means I can’t stop. I haven’t really timed it or anything.
Do you feel a strong need to arrange the boxes in a specific way, even if it's not required for your job?

Yeah… I mean, it feels like I’m supposed to put them a certain way, even if nobody wrote it on the sheet or anything. But then it gets weird because I’ll start making these little patterns with the boxes, like turning them or setting them in rows that make sense to me, and people are yelling, “Stop, that’s not where that goes.”

And sometimes I just kind of freeze there by the forklift with my arms up, like I’m halfway through doing the hand signal, and then I hear the backup beeper and I’ll copy it without really meaning to. That’s what they keep bringing up, I think. My supervisor said it wasn’t even about the boxes being required anymore, it was me doing strange stuff when everyone needed me to move out of the way.

It reminds me of those crosswalk signals that beep different in different neighborhoods—sorry, I know that’s not what you asked. But yeah, I guess I do get stuck on doing it a specific way, even when it’s not part of the job.
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions or behaviors over and over again?

Yeah, sort of… I mean, I don’t count like “one, two, three” or anything. But at work they say I keep doing the same kinds of things again, like I’ll get stuck with my arms up by the forklift, like I’m frozen in the middle of a hand signal, and then if the beeper goes off I might copy the sound without really thinking.

And the boxes… I’ll move them into these little patterns, or turn them a certain way, even when people are yelling for me to stop because it’s not helping. It’s like my body keeps going back to it.

The forklift beeping is really loud in that warehouse, though, and it kind of gets in your head. Like the crosswalk noises near the bus stop, they’re all different depending on where you are, and sometimes I notice that more than what I’m supposed to be doing… but yeah, I guess there are things I repeat.
Do you believe that the patterns you see have any special powers or abilities?

Special powers? I don’t know… I wouldn’t say powers like, like a movie or something. I just notice them and they seem important in the moment.

Like the way boxes line up, or how the floor tiles make these paths—well, the tiles at the grocery store near my apartment are different from the ones by the bus stop, and that always makes me think about how people decide those layouts. It’s probably just some manager picking whatever’s cheapest, right?

So… no, I don’t think they have powers. I just get caught up in them sometimes.
Do you ever have thoughts that keep coming into your mind even when you don't want them to?

I’m not sure what counts as that. Like, everybody has stuff pop in their head, right? A song from the radio or remembering you forgot milk or whatever.

Sometimes I’ll get stuck thinking about something, but I don’t know if it’s “unwanted” exactly. Like the sound of the lights in the break room, or the way the carts at the store all pull to one side—there’s this one grocery cart wheel that makes that wobble sound, and then I’m thinking about who fixes those, if anyone even checks them.

Sorry, I’m kind of going off. I guess… I haven’t really noticed thoughts coming in that I’m trying to fight off like that. I’d have to think about what you mean.
Do you feel like your need to arrange things in a certain way is causing you a lot of stress or anxiety?

I don’t know if it’s anxiety exactly. I mean, people keep saying I’m messing things up at the warehouse because I’ll move the boxes into these weird little patterns, and then they’re yelling, “Stop, stop,” and I’m still doing it for a second.

It’s more like I get stuck. Like with the forklift, I’ll have my arms up doing the signal and then just kind of freeze there, and the beeper goes off and I might copy it without meaning to. The beepers are really sharp, though, like they cut through everything, and then everyone looks at you like you did it on purpose.

So… yeah, it causes problems. Stress, I guess, because people get mad and I don’t always know how to stop right away.
Do you feel like your behaviors or thoughts about patterns are affecting your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it does. Not just friends or family exactly, but people around me. At work they took me off forklift stuff, like I’m not doing those duties anymore, because they said it wasn’t safe or they couldn’t count on me to keep things moving right.

And school too—my community college classes, I’m behind now. I keep meaning to catch up, but then the assignments all kind of pile up like boxes, you know, and once they’re stacked wrong it’s hard to… anyway.

I stopped going to the church food-bank shifts too. I used to help there, carrying things and sorting cans—there’s always so many dented cans, and people put the labels facing different ways—but they said they needed people they could rely on. So yeah, I think people don’t really trust me the same now.
Do you think that the patterns you see or the things that happen around you are somehow specifically related to you or your life?

I don’t know. I mean, related to me like… on purpose? I haven’t really thought of it that way.

Sometimes things line up in a way that catches my attention, like the boxes or the labels or the lights buzzing, and then I get stuck looking at it. But I don’t know if that means it’s about my life. It might just be… things are arranged badly, or too loud, or people leave stuff crooked and then everyone acts like you’re the one making it weird.

Sorry, I’m not answering right. I don’t really know if it’s specifically related to me.
Do you think that things happening around you, like the patterns or the noises, are sending you a message or are specifically about you?

I’m not sure. Like, “message” feels like a strong word. Sometimes the noises feel… important, I guess, because they won’t let me think past them, but I don’t know if they’re saying something to me.

At work there was this one machine that made this repeating clank, and I kept counting it, but then somebody dropped a pallet and everyone got mad because I wasn’t moving fast enough. And my cousin has this old truck that makes a similar sound when it starts, so I was thinking about that, and then—sorry, I’m getting off.

I don’t really know if it’s about me. It just feels hard to ignore when it happens.
Do you believe that there are messages or meanings in the patterns or noises that are specifically intended for you?

I don’t know if they’re intended for me. That sounds like… like somebody made them for me, and I can’t say that.

I notice them, though. Like if a fan is clicking or the floor tiles make a line that doesn’t match up, I’ll get stuck on it, but I don’t really know that it means something. Sometimes I think maybe I’m supposed to fix it, like straighten it out, but then that’s just because it bothers me.

The other day there was this stack of crates, and one was turned the wrong way, and I kept thinking about it after, even when I was trying to do something else. But a message? I don’t know. I don’t think I can say that.
Do you feel like you have to perform certain actions or rituals in a specific order or way to feel right or to prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t know if it’s like a ritual, exactly. I don’t think I’m trying to stop something bad, not like that.

But at the warehouse I guess I do get stuck doing things a certain way. Like I’ll move boxes into these little patterns, and people start yelling because it’s not where they’re supposed to go. Or I’ll freeze for a second with my arms up by the forklift, like I’m waiting for the next signal, and then I realize everybody’s looking at me.

Sometimes the forklift beeps and I kind of copy it, or I copy the hand signals, and then it just keeps going in my head. I’m not trying to mess things up. It just feels like if I don’t do it the right way, I can’t move on, but I don’t know if that’s the same as preventing something bad.
Do you feel like you must do things in a certain way or order to feel okay?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if it’s “must,” but at work I get caught doing it a certain way, like with the boxes. I’ll start moving them into these little patterns, and even when people are yelling that it’s wrong, I’m still trying to make it feel… lined up, I guess.

And by the forklift I’ve frozen with my arms up before, like I’m stuck waiting for the next hand signal. The beeping gets in my head too, and sometimes I copy it without really meaning to. That’s part of why they got upset with me at the warehouse, I think.

It’s more like I get stuck. Like with the forklift, I’ll have my arms up doing the signal and then just kind of freeze there, and the beeper goes off and I might copy it without meaning to. The beepers are really sharp, though, like they cut through everything, and then everyone looks at you like you did it on purpose.

So… yeah, it causes problems. Stress, I guess, because people get mad and I don’t always know how to stop right away.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning due to their symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel like your behaviors or thoughts about patterns are affecting your relationships with friends or family?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve lost my forklift duties, fallen behind in my community-college classes, and stopped showing up for the church food-bank shifts because people say they can’t count on me or keep things safe around me anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the behaviors or thoughts about patterns are affecting relationships and daily functioning; this is most directly covered by the functional impairment profile, which includes problems with work, school, and social/community reliability.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I guess it does. Not just friends or family exactly, but people around me. At work they took me off forklift stuff, like I’m not doing those duties anymore, because they said it wasn’t safe or they couldn’t count on me to keep things moving right.

And school too—my community college classes, I’m behind now. I keep meaning to catch up, but then the assignments all kind of pile up like boxes, you know, and once they’re stacked wrong it’s hard to… anyway.

I stopped going to the church food-bank shifts too. I used to help there, carrying things and sorting cans—there’s always so many dented cans, and people put the labels facing different ways—but they said they needed people they could rely on. So yeah, I think people don’t really trust me the same now.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions of reference
doctor.question: Do you think that the patterns you see or the things that happen around you are somehow specifically related to you or your life?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about ideas of reference or whether external patterns/events feel personally related to the patient, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know. I mean, related to me like… on purpose? I haven’t really thought of it that way.

Sometimes things line up in a way that catches my attention, like the boxes or the labels or the lights buzzing, and then I get stuck looking at it. But I don’t know if that means it’s about my life. It might just be… things are arranged badly, or too loud, or people leave stuff crooked and then everyone acts like you’re the one making it weird.

Sorry, I’m not answering right. I don’t really know if it’s specifically related to me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions of reference
doctor.question: Do you think that things happening around you, like the patterns or the noises, are sending you a message or are specifically about you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether patterns or noises feel like messages or are specifically about the patient, which relates to ideas of reference or delusional interpretation. This symptom is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. Like, “message” feels like a strong word. Sometimes the noises feel… important, I guess, because they won’t let me think past them, but I don’t know if they’re saying something to me.

At work there was this one machine that made this repeating clank, and I kept counting it, but then somebody dropped a pallet and everyone got mad because I wasn’t moving fast enough. And my cousin has this old truck that makes a similar sound when it starts, so I was thinking about that, and then—sorry, I’m getting off.

I don’t really know if it’s about me. It just feels hard to ignore when it happens.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of delusions
doctor.question: Do you believe that there are messages or meanings in the patterns or noises that are specifically intended for you?

target_item.reason: The question asks about believing patterns or noises contain messages specifically intended for me, which is an idea of reference/delusional meaning. That symptom is not included in the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if they’re intended for me. That sounds like… like somebody made them for me, and I can’t say that.

I notice them, though. Like if a fan is clicking or the floor tiles make a line that doesn’t match up, I’ll get stuck on it, but I don’t really know that it means something. Sometimes I think maybe I’m supposed to fix it, like straighten it out, but then that’s just because it bothers me.

The other day there was this stack of crates, and one was turned the wrong way, and I kept thinking about it after, even when I was trying to do something else. But a message? I don’t know. I don’t think I can say that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences compulsions to perform specific rituals or behaviors
doctor.question: Do you feel like you have to perform certain actions or rituals in a specific order or way to feel right or to prevent something bad from happening?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I guess they brought me in because at the warehouse I keep doing things like freezing with my arms up by the forklift, copying the beeping sounds and hand signals, or moving boxes in strange little patterns even when everyone is yelling for me to stop.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about ritualized actions done in a specific order or way; the closest covered profile item is the patient's abnormal/disorganized behavior involving moving boxes in strange patterns and freezing/copying actions at the warehouse.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if it’s like a ritual, exactly. I don’t think I’m trying to stop something bad, not like that.

But at the warehouse I guess I do get stuck doing things a certain way. Like I’ll move boxes into these little patterns, and people start yelling because it’s not where they’re supposed to go. Or I’ll freeze for a second with my arms up by the forklift, like I’m waiting for the next signal, and then I realize everybody’s looking at me.

Sometimes the forklift beeps and I kind of copy it, or I copy the hand signals, and then it just keeps going in my head. I’m not trying to mess things up. It just feels like if I don’t do it the right way, I can’t move on, but I don’t know if that’s the same as preventing something bad.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences compulsions to perform specific rituals or actions
doctor.question: Do you feel like you must do things in a certain way or order to feel okay?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I guess they brought me in because at the warehouse I keep doing things like freezing with my arms up by the forklift, copying the beeping sounds and hand signals, or moving boxes in strange little patterns even when everyone is yelling for me to stop.
target_item.reason: The question asks about needing to do actions in a certain way or order, which matches the described abnormal behavior of moving boxes in strange patterns, freezing, and copying sounds or signals at the warehouse.

patient.answer:
Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if it’s “must,” but at work I get caught doing it a certain way, like with the boxes. I’ll start moving them into these little patterns, and even when people are yelling that it’s wrong, I’m still trying to make it feel… lined up, I guess.

And by the forklift I’ve frozen with my arms up before, like I’m stuck waiting for the next hand signal. The beeping gets in my head too, and sometimes I copy it without really meaning to. That’s part of why they got upset with me at the warehouse, I think.
